title: Minimal critical groups of McKay quivers: Gaetz's Question 2 settled for n = 3 (computer-assisted), conjectured for n >= 4
statement: Let gamma: G -> SL_n(C) be a faithful representation of a finite group without trivial constituent. Theorem 9 (computer-assisted): for n = 3, the BKR surjection K(gamma) ->> (G^ab)^ is an isomorphism iff chi_gamma is real-valued and G is dihedral of order 2m with m >= 3 odd, A_4 or A_5 (rotation groups in SO(3)). Ingredients: Proposition 3, |K(gamma)| = 2^(u-1)|G~^ab| for G in SO(3) (u = number of classes of the preimage G~ in SU(2) equal to their negatives), giving a uniform proof of Gaetz's SO(3) classification (Theorem 4); Lemma 6 (abelian product bound) and Theorem 7 (monomial types C, D: analytic reduction to diagonal part of order <= 75, exact enumeration of 70 groups); Theorem 8 (reducible type B: central-factor bound, dihedral reduction to order <= 46 or the real dihedral family, 18 exceptional groups computed); Proposition 5 (primitive types E-L computed; only A_5 minimal); abelian type A is BKR Proposition 6.19. Theorem M (proved by hand, no hypotheses on determinants, dimensions or reality): for gamma_1 faithful and gamma_2 ANY representation, |K(gamma_1 + gamma_2)| >= |K(gamma_1)|, with equality iff gamma_2 is a multiple of the trivial representation; hence a minimal gamma has no faithful proper summand OF DETERMINANT 1 after deleting trivial summands (Corollary M1; the determinant hypothesis is necessary because (F1) is a statement about representations into SL_n and fails without it, smallest failure Z/2 with the sign character, |K| = 1 < 2), and |K(gamma_1 + gamma_2)| >= |K(gamma_1)| + |K(gamma_2)| for two faithful summands (Corollary M2, tight). The proof rests on Lemma A: conjugating nI - M by the diagonal matrix of irreducible degrees turns the McKay-Cartan matrix into the Laplacian of a weighted digraph with arc weights M_ij delta_j / delta_i, so |K(gamma)| is the weighted count of arborescences of the McKay quiver rooted at the trivial vertex; and Proposition B: the count rooted at chi_v is delta_v^2 times that one, which re-proves the order formula (F3) by elementary linear algebra. Lemma 2 (the earlier sector form, now superseded) proved the strict inequality only when det gamma_1 = det gamma_2 = 1 and chi_1 is real-valued or 1/n_1 + 1/n_2 >= 1/2, via the sector lemma: for U in SU(n), n - tr U lies in |arg| <= pi/2 - pi/n. Conjecture 10 (Gaetz's Question 2 for n >= 4): no minimal gamma with n >= 4.
resolves: Gaetz's Question 2 (honors thesis, 2016) / BKR Question 6.11 in dimension 3 (computer-assisted written argument, pending specialist review)
verified: check_mckay_minimal.py (GAP + Python): SO(3) formula and classification (cyclic/dihedral m <= 12, A4, S4, A5); primitive SL3 table; exhaustive scan of all groups of order <= 24 with n <= 5; ATLAS tables A5, 2.A5, L2(7), S5, A6, 2.A6 with n <= 6; analytic finite regions of Theorems 7-8 (bounds_check.py); monomial enumeration reproduced (47 type C, 23 type D; minimal only C3 with trivial constituent, S3, A4); GAP recomputation of enumerated monomial groups of order <= 60; the 18 exceptional type B groups (minimal only inside SL2).

Exhaustive SmallGroups scans (faithful, det 1, no trivial constituent): all groups of order <= 40 with n <= 5; non-abelian groups of order <= 71 with n <= 6; all 3595 non-abelian groups of order <= 150 with n = 3; all 3117 non-abelian groups of order 72..150 with n <= 4. Minimal cases exactly as predicted; no case below the BKR bound; none with n >= 4.
47 ATLAS character tables with n <= 8: minimal only for A5 (n = 3) and 2.A5 (n = 2).
Monomial enumeration cross-checked against GAP matrix groups for all 59 enumerated groups of order <= 220.
Independent agent review of 0.1.0 (Lemmas 1-2, Proposition 3, Theorem 4): proofs correct; wording fixes applied in 0.2.0.
Independent agent review of 0.2.0 (Lemma 6, Theorems 7-9): no mathematical error; notation (X' in type D), tail arguments of the bounds, and several justifications made explicit in 0.3.0.

Monotonicity search: 1,359,437 pairs (gamma_1 faithful det 1, gamma_2 det 1 nontrivial, dimensions <= 4, non-abelian groups of order <= 60), no violation of |K(gamma_1 + gamma_2)| > |K(gamma_1)|; sector_check.py checks the edge inequality numerically for n <= 10.

arborescence_check.g (gate ARBORESCENCE): on all groups of order <= 24 with at most 6 conjugacy classes and all representations of degree <= 4 without trivial constituent, in exact arithmetic -- Lemma A (372 cases), the order formula of Proposition B (372), Proposition B(i)'s delta_v^2 ratio (1545 vertex checks), and Theorem M's row expansion with every mixed term nonnegative together with the strictness witness and the strict inequality (24584 pairs each); 0 failures. A wider run (order <= 48, at most 8 classes, degrees <= 5) was attempted with an earlier version of the same script; it ran about 100 minutes, emitted no failure line, and was then cut off by its own timeout without writing a summary, so it is NOT claimed and no evidence file records it. The independent review covers that range by other means.

super.g: Corollary M2 on 45 groups of order <= 48 with at most 9 classes and degrees <= 5, with no determinant condition: 4,632,464 pairwise and 120,613 three-fold tests, 0 failures; minimum slack 0, so the bound is tight.
mono2.g: Theorem M itself (the inequality and the equality case) with no determinant condition on either summand, over SmallGroups -- see evidence/raw/monotonicity_unconditional_le48.txt.

m1_hypothesis_check.g (gate M1_HYPOTHESIS): among the faithful representations of degree <= 3 of the groups of order <= 20, all 591 with det = 1 satisfy |K| >= |G^ab| as (F1) requires, while 136 of the 10,963 with det != 1 do not. This pins the determinant hypothesis of Corollary M1 as necessary; it was found by checking Corollary M1 against Theorem 8 rather than by the gate.

Independent review of the arborescence section (fresh agent, own GAP exporter and own Python checkers: Bareiss determinant, Smith normal form, Faddeev-LeVerrier characteristic polynomial, arborescence enumeration over exact rationals; |K| taken from its own SNF, never from the product formula or from arborescences). Verdict: Lemma A correct; Proposition B's conclusions correct; Theorem M correct and unbroken in 157,232 pairs with no determinant or reality restriction (including 99,296+ with non-real character, 53,126+ with some M_ii > 0, 29,782+ where gamma_2 mixes trivial with nontrivial constituents, 46,463+ abelian, dimension pairs up to (12,2) and (7,7)); Corollary M2 correct. It confirmed independently that Corollary M1 was false as stated in 0.4.0 (330 counterexamples up to order 32 and 254 more up to order 64, 0 after adding det gamma_1 = 1), and found one error this dossier had missed: the x^1 coefficient claims in Proposition B were both off by (-1)^l. Also verified: det C = A_0 on 9420 representations, A_v = delta_v^2 det C on all of them including the 3593 non-faithful ones, the order formula on 27,495 records, det C = 0 for all 8798 non-faithful records, the upper bound det C <= prod (n - M_ii) on 17,730, and the full S-expansion on 4000 pairs with no negative term. Its arborescence-level checks were exhaustive on the order <= 32 set; the larger sets were checked via the order formula, SNF and Theorem M itself.
unresolved: read arXiv:1704.03778 (Grinberg-Huang-Reiner) from the end of section 6 onwards: the fetch tools truncate there and the authors' copy is robots_disallowed, so novelty of Lemma A, Proposition B and Theorem M is not asserted
specialist review (agent reviews only so far; the sector form of Lemma 2 is unreviewed; the arborescence section had one agent review in 0.4.2)
Theorem 9 depends on Blichfeldt's classification of finite subgroups of SL3(C) (as tabulated by Yau-Yu)
structure of K beyond its order outside the cases computed by Gaetz
nonclaims: the SO(3) classification (Theorem 4) is Gaetz's Theorem 8(ii); only the uniform proof via Proposition 3 is offered as new
the abelian case is BKR Proposition 6.19
the conjecture for n >= 4 is Gaetz's Question 2; no proof for n >= 4
Theorems 7-9 are computer-assisted: analytic bounds plus exact finite computation; not a novelty determination
no novelty is asserted for Lemma A, Proposition B, Theorem M or Corollaries M1 and M2: one source (arXiv:1704.03778) has not been read to the end. They are recorded as proved, not as new.

Theorem M does not bear on Conjecture 10 beyond Corollary M1: minimality is the rational identity A_0 = |G^ab| and is not a combinatorial smallness condition on the quiver (for A_5 with its 3-dimensional representation A_0 = 1 while several arborescences have positive weight).
smallest_decisive_test: A faithful representation into SL_n (n >= 4) without trivial constituent with |K(gamma)| = |G^ab|; or an error in the finite regions of Theorems 7-8 (a monomial group with diagonal part of order > 75, or a type B group of order > 46 outside the listed families, that is minimal).
